text:
zoe: quick sync: we need a clear split for quota/rate enforcement across hosted/dedicated/private before we merge the hosting RFC. raising a few concrete proposals.

elaine: agree. current idea is: hosted -> control-plane preflight + runtime final check; dedicated -> runtime authoritative; private -> runtime authoritative with signed policy bundles (allow offline enforcement).

sam: for hosted preflight we must keep admission latency tiny (<5ms). router should cache recent admission decisions per-tenant. eviction: LRU keyed by tenant with token-bucket refill aligned to billing windows.

marco: routing + counting hazards: if router falls back from hosted to dedicated, we can double-count. solve with an admission_id flow: router requests admission_id from control-plane, forwards it to runtime, runtime includes admission_id in usage reports. control-plane dedupes on admission_id.

anya: private/offline case: runtime should accept signed policy bundles (policy.json + sig + version + ttl). bundles say whether runtime may issue local admissions and the offline budget. defaults: bundle TTL 24h, admission TTL 5s, offline allowance 1h cumulative.

zoe: security: admission_id must not embed tenant names. use HMAC(router_key, nonce||ts) and keep keys rotated quarterly. runtime accepts current + previous key for a grace period.

elaine: error normalization: clients always see 429 with structured details {reason, origin: controlplane|runtime, admission_id, retry_after}. SDKs map that to QuotaError. add header X-Redwood-Quota-Origin for debugging.

sam: fallback hints from runtime: structured metadata like {fallback: "dedicated" | "degraded-model" | "retry_after": secs}. router chooses next target based on tenant permissions and runtime capability flags.

marco: runtime capability advert: supports_admission_id, supports_fallback, consumption_precision (estimated|exact). router uses this to pick compatible targets.

anya: reconciliation API: runtime posts usage reports [{admission_id, tokens, ts}]. control-plane dedupes by admission_id, verifies locally-signed tokens only if bundle allowed offline issuance and within offline budget.

zoe: tests: 1) simulate hosted->dedicated fallback to ensure single admission counted, 2) private offline enforcement and later reconcile respecting budget, 3) router key rotation acceptance.

elaine: telemetry hooks: admission_latency_ms, admission_cache_hit, admission_origin, reconcile_lag_seconds, offline_budget_remaining. console: show bundle age and offline budget warnings for private tenants.

ops-bot: deploy: admission-proto canary rolled by @sam to staging (runtime v1.20.0).

zoe: i'll draft the RFC follow-up with header names, bundle schema, admission flow pseudo-code, reconciliation API, and recommended TTLs. pinging @elaine @sam @marco @anya for review.

elaine: TL;DR: split enforcement by hosting trust model, normalize client errors, use admission ids + signed bundles for offline, and add reconciliation + telemetry.
